transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-28
Start: 10:00 PT (15:00Z)
Duration: ~52 minutes
Recording ID: ff-20270228-krp-8421
Attendees: Jenna (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya, Tomás, Elliot

Summary (auto):
Krypton is evaluating open model options for product search, chat, and inventory tool-calling. Key constraints: very long product context (consolidated descriptions + user history ~20k-60k tokens), multilingual (EN/ES/PT), tight latency in checkout flow, and strict PII/PCI considerations. They want Hosted for initial testing, Dedicated or Private for production depending on compliance.

00:00 Jenna: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. i'm jenna from Redwood Inference, account exec. quick round of intros?
00:12 Priya: priya here, head of ai at krypton. we run recommendations and chat for web + mobile, also powering store assistants.
00:20 Tomás: tomás, infra/platform. i'll own networking/security for any pilot.
:27 Elliot: elliot, product — focused on checkout user flows and conversational product search.
00:35 Marcus: marcus, se at redwood, i'll dig into latency and model tradeoffs. nice to meet you.

01:02 Jenna: high-level, is the primary goal to replace your current semantic search or to add chat-with-inventory that can call tools? or both?
01:15 Priya: both, ideally. semantic search for product discovery, but chat that can call into inventory API for availability and do returns/fulfillment tasks. so tool-calling is a must.
01:30 Marcus: good. any numbers on average product doc size or the context you need in a single request?
01:38 Priya: typical product descriptions are 2-4 paragraphs but we also want to pass recent user session history and related SKUs — median payloads now around 8k tokens but peak use cases reach 40k, esp when doing cross-sell explanations and combining catalog+reviews.
01:58 Tomás: and for multilingual — we need spanish and portuguese support, plus EN obviously.
02:06 Marcus: ok that helps. so we have three levers w.r.t model/runtime: hosted small-context low-latency, dedicated with higher batching for throughput, and private (VPC/on-prem) for full data residency. for 40k peaks we usually recommend model variants with long context (32k/64k) or context-window stitching with prefix/KV cache.

02:45 Priya: can you clarify context-window stitching? does that lose info?
02:52 Marcus: yes, so quick explainer — we do prefix caching and KV cache reuse for chat tokens, and you can stream in chunks. for factual cross-checks we use reranking + embeddings to pull top candidates from the catalog so you don't need the entire catalog in prompt. but for some product explanation threads you may want a model with native 64k window or a retrieval-augmented approach. sometimes a hybrid is best.
03:25 Jenna: note: krypton cares about latency in checkout — 300-400ms token latency target for user-visible flows.

03:40 Elliot: 300-400ms seems tight — is that realistic if we run a 32k window model?
03:48 Marcus: it's a tradeoff — model size and quantization matter. a trimmed Llama-derivative 32k quantized to int8 on Dedicated GPUs can hit interactive latencies within that range for shorter responses; for longer responses or 64k windows latency grows. we can route critical checkout calls to small fast models and relegated explanation-heavy queries to higher-context backends. Redwood routing supports that.

04:20 Priya: what open models do you recommend? we've evaluated Mistral, Llama 2/3, MPT variants, and Mixtral internally.
04:32 Marcus: for multilingual and long-context, we typically recommend: mixtral for instruction-following with 32k, llama-3 variants for strong instruction tuning but check shipping sizes, and Mistral 7B-instruct for cost-performance on standard tasks. for 64k native windows, some forks/variants of llama and custom long-context models are better — we can provide a compatibility matrix.
04:58 Priya: any weird name mismatches — sorry i misread some docs where you said Redwood dedicated vs redwood dev?
05:04 Jenna: yeah, docs can be confusing. "Redwood Dedicated" = reserved GPU pools; "Redwood Private" = VPC or on-prem boxed control plane. we'll send a one-pager.

05:20 Tomás: security question — we handle payment tokens and PII. would Hosted be a non-starter?
05:28 Marcus: depends on your risk appetite. Hosted can be used with strong anonymization and data retention controls; if PCI or strict audit logs are required, many customers go Dedicated or Private and integrate KMS/HSM for key control and retention. Redwood supports audit logs and RBAC. we'll include SOC2/ISO artifacts in the security pack.

06:05 Elliot: tool-calling — do you support function or tool-calling like openai-style or is it a custom layer?
06:12 Marcus: we support structured tool-calling patterns through a standard schema; a bit of a mix — function-calling is supported for hosted models that expose that feature and for private we let you bake in connectors. we also support reranking via embeddings pipelines and can handle mid-flight KV cache for tool access.

06:44 Priya: about cost — how do you suggest we price plan for peaks? our traffic is spiky during promotions.
06:53 Jenna: many retailers use Dedicated with autoscaling + burst capacity. you get predictable baseline with committed pools and pay for bursts. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and caching settings for promo windows to keep unit cost down. we'll include examples in the follow-up.

07:20 Tomás: do you have benchmarks for 32k vs 64k on nv4 vs h100? or is that in your public catalog?
07:29 Marcus: we have verified performance profiles per model/hardware. public catalog shows numbers but for your workload we'll run a benchmark on a sanitized sample. need your sample and a few typical prompt templates.

08:02 Priya: we can sanitize some rows but reviews contain PII sometimes — we'll need guidance on redaction.
08:10 Jenna: we'll share a redaction checklist and sample sanitization script.

08:28 Elliot: what about multilingual embeddings — do you recommend a single multilingual embed model or language-specific?
08:34 Marcus: single multilingual embeddings usually ok; but for fine-grained semantic recall, language-specific models can edge out. depends on corpus size. for now we'd prototype with a multilingual 2k-4k embedding and see recall performance.

09:00 Priya: i want to understand failure modes. if the dedicated pool is busy, does it failover to hosted?
09:07 Marcus: yes, we can set routing policies that fall back to hosted or to a cheaper model variant. that's part of graceful degradation. we can also set per-route SLOs and throttles to protect checkout flows.

09:30 Tomás: compliance — we'll need SSO (SAML/Okta) and audit logs. also need to know where logs live and retention controls.
09:38 Jenna: included — Dedicated/Private have configurable log retention; Private gives you customer-controlled storage. we'll attach the compliance doc.

10:05 Priya: POC scope — we want: 1) benchmark on sanitized product catalog (32k/40k patterns), 2) pilot chat + tool-calling for inventory check, 3) multilang evaluation on EN/ES/PT. duration 4 weeks. is that reasonable?
10:21 Marcus: reasonable. for the benchmark we need sample schema and a list of endpoints to mimic. we'll propose a test harness.

10:40 Jenna: ok recap and next steps: jenna to send pricing + security pack, marcus to run initial latency table once sample arrives, priya/tomás to share samples and compliance constraints, schedule POC kickoff week of 2027-03-07.

10:55 Elliot: sounds good. quick Q — are there demo templates for retail tool-calling?
11:02 Marcus: yes, we'll share a small demo repo that shows tool-calling patterns and an example reranker pipeline. link in follow-up.

11:18 Priya: thanks all. appreciate the clarity.
11:22 Jenna: thank you. we'll follow up by end of week with docs and links.

(End of meeting)

Notes: occasional transcription glitches — "kayvee cache" for KV cache, "Redwood dev" heard in places but meant Redwood Dedicated. Shared artifacts: /links/security-pack.pdf, /links/benchmark-template.xlsx, github.com/redwood-examples/retail-tool-calling (links to be included in follow-up email).
